findings.description: A new Historic Resource Review by Page & Turnbull, published ahead of plans to replace the Golden Gate University campus with the city's fifth- or sixth-tallest skyscraper, found the 1979 Brutalist addition at 536 Mission Street eligible for the California Register under Criterion 3 (architectural merit) for its expressive massing, sunken plaza, pedestrian bridge and total landscape design. The campus's earlier 1923 commercial building, at Mission and Ecker, was found in a 2007 review (Kelley & VerPlanck) too altered to retain integrity. The 1979 addition was designed by William D. Podesto & Associates with consulting engineer T.Y. Lin.

findings.description: The century-old former Edward McRoskey Mattress Factory at 1687 Market Street has been torn down ahead of a 17-storey, 182-foot affordable housing tower and artist community hub; the application was filed in mid-2024, won final approval in March 2025, and demolition permits were filed in July 2025 and issued in November, with crews starting in early February 2026. Built in 1925 by architects Fabre & Hildebrand in a classical revival style for the 1899-founded McRoskey company (the family still operates it as McRoskey Airflex Mattress Company). Mercy Housing is developing it on behalf of the Artists Hub on Market; Mark Cavagnero Associates designed the replacement with landscape architect Shades of Green.

extra.developer_of_proposal: Mercy Housing, for the Artists Hub on Market
extra.demolished_building: Edward McRoskey Mattress Factory, built 1925 by Fabre & Hildebrand, classical revival

findings.description: The Planning Commission reviewed the Draft Environmental Impact Report for Freedom West 2.0, a master plan to replace the existing Freedom West cooperative with 2,291 apartments (including replacement units for existing residents), 15 buildings up to 335 feet, retail and a 150-key hotel across three phases; Phase One (five buildings, 935 units) centers on 880 McAllister Street. The original 1970s Freedom West co-op was sponsored by Bethel African Methodist Episcopal Church -- Rev. J. Austell Hall of Bethel A.M.E. is credited in the EIR's historic review as its key figure, responding to "the eroding character of the Fillmore" with a resident-owned co-op -- and designed by Krisel Shapiro & Associates. MacFarlane Partners is the applicant, working with Avanath Capital Management; DLR Group is project architect and master planner, with Kimley Horn as civil engineer.
